abstract.t: Status: proposed. Module: std/net/multipart.ts (nish/net/multipart). A reader of the multipart/form-data bodies an HTML form sends (RFC 7578), framed as RFC 2046 Section 5.1.1 frames every multipart body. This spec holds the reader to the binding sentences of those sections that a receiver can be held to, and to the refusals nish adds, through three functions that read a whole body: multipartPartCount, multipartFieldData and multipartFieldFilename.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.

A server that takes a file upload reads a multipart/form-data body. RFC 7578 defines its parts and RFC 2046 its framing. Most of their binding sentences bind the sender: what a boundary may not appear in, which parameters a part carries, how several files are sent. This spec quotes the ones a receiver can be held to, and states the rest of what the reader does in its own words.

The module reads each part with MultipartReader, a class, and the functions below read a whole body with it and its default MultipartLimits, so every requirement here holds of the class as each function reaches it.
Out of scope: MultipartReader, a class that vector does not call; the three functions of this spec read every part through it.
Out of scope: MultipartLimits, a class of three limits; this spec reads with its defaults, 64 parts, 16 header lines and 8192 octets of them.

This spec does not cover RFC 7578's percent-encoded or non-ASCII field names (Section 5.1), the _charset_ field (Section 4.6), a part's Content-Transfer-Encoding (Section 4.7), which the reader does not apply, or the older multipart/mixed form of several files for one field (Section 4.3), which it reads as one part with a multipart/mixed Content-Type.

section.name: Interface
section.sourcecode: // module: nish/net/multipart export const multipartPartCount = (body: u8[], boundary: string): i32 export const multipartFieldData = (body: u8[], boundary: string, name: string): u8[] | null export const multipartFieldFilename = (body: u8[], boundary: string, name: string): string | null
section.t: Each function reads all of body as the message body, and boundary is the boundary parameter of its Content-Type, quotes removed. A body in this spec is written as the ASCII text of its octets.

section.name: Delimiters

blockquote.t: The boundary delimiter MUST occur at the beginning of a line, i.e., following a CRLF, and the initial CRLF is considered to be attached to the boundary delimiter line rather than part of the preceding part.

section.t: The first delimiter may open the body with no CRLF before it. For a body that ends in its close delimiter, multipartPartCount MUST return how many parts the body holds.
The octets before the first delimiter and after the close delimiter MUST be skipped.
Spaces and tabs between a delimiter and its CRLF, RFC 2046's transport padding, MUST be skipped.
A CRLF, two hyphens and the boundary followed by anything but transport padding and a CRLF, or two more hyphens, MUST be read as data.

section.name: Header fields
section.t: A part's header field names MUST be matched without regard to case.
RFC 7578 Section 4.8 bars a sender from other header fields. A header field other than Content-Disposition and Content-Type MUST be ignored.

section.name: Disposition

blockquote.t: Each part MUST contain a Content-Disposition header field [RFC2183] where the disposition type is "form-data".

The Content-Disposition header field MUST also contain an additional parameter of "name"; the value of the "name" parameter is the original field name from the form (possibly encoded; see Section 5.1).

section.t: The disposition type MUST be matched without regard to case.

section.name: Data
section.t: multipartFieldData MUST return the data of the first part whose name is name, octet for octet: every octet from the empty line that ends its header fields to the CRLF of the delimiter after it.
multipartFieldData and multipartFieldFilename MUST return null when no part before the close delimiter has that name, and when the body is refused before one does.

section.name: File names
section.t: multipartFieldFilename MUST return the filename parameter of the first part whose name is name as the sender wrote it, quotes removed: a backslash inside the quotes is an octet like any other, so a Windows path such as C:\x.txt keeps its backslash, and a browser's escaped quote %22a%22.txt stays as given.
multipartFieldFilename MUST return null for a part with no filename parameter.
A filename* parameter MUST NOT be read in place of filename.

section.name: Refusals
section.t: multipartPartCount returns one of these codes for a body it refuses:

li.t: -4: a part has too many header lines or octets of them;
-6: the body has too many parts.

section.t: multipartPartCount MUST return -1 for a boundary that is empty, longer than 70 octets, holds an octet outside RFC 2046's bchars or ends in a space.
multipartPartCount MUST return -2 for a body with no opening delimiter, or whose part's header lines or data run to its end.
multipartPartCount MUST return -3 for a header line that ends in a CR or LF alone, starts with a space or tab, or has no colon, and for a part with two Content-Type fields.
multipartPartCount MUST return -4 for a part with more than 16 header lines, or more than 8192 octets of them.
multipartPartCount MUST return -5 for a part with no Content-Disposition, two of them, one whose type is not form-data, or one with no name parameter.
multipartPartCount MUST return -6 for a body of more than 64 parts.

section.name: Test Vectors
section.t: Each row's body is checked against the multipart reader of Python's email package.

tr.td: a field and a file, as a browser sends them
a preamble, padding, a boundary mid-line and an epilogue
the CRLF before a delimiter is the delimiter's, the one before it the data's
a longer boundary after a CRLF and two hyphens is data

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: A body is read from the network, so a sender picks every octet of it. The reader copies no part's data, finds a delimiter by comparing at most the boundary's length plus six octets at each CR of the body, and holds each part's header lines to MultipartLimits, so a body of n octets and a boundary of b octets costs about n * (b + 6) comparisons at most, however it is shaped. docs/security/net-multipart.md records the reader's review.

front.title: Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions (MIME) Part Two: Media Types

abstract.t: This second document defines the general structure of the MIME media typing system and defines an initial set of media types. [STANDARDS-TRACK]

This specification defines the multipart/form-data media type, which can be used by a wide variety of applications and transported by a wide variety of protocols as a way of returning a set of values as the result of a user filling out a form. This document obsoletes RFC 2388.

front.title: Key words for use in RFCs to Indicate Requirement Levels

abstract.t: In many standards track documents several words are used to signify the requirements in the specification. These words are often capitalized. This document defines these words as they should be interpreted in IETF documents. This document specifies an Internet Best Current Practices for the Internet Community, and requests discussion and suggestions for improvements.

front.title: Ambiguity of Uppercase vs Lowercase in RFC 2119 Key Words

abstract.t: RFC 2119 specifies common key words that may be used in protocol specifications. This document aims to reduce the ambiguity by clarifying that only UPPERCASE usage of the key words have the defined special meanings.
